issues.description: import-notation 'url' branch inverts the early-return logic and skips the validation it was meant to perform.
issues.detail: Under primary='url', the guard returns when params contain 'url(', short-circuiting the very case the rule should check. The string branch is correct (skip when nothing to check); the url branch should mirror it. Also verify a quoted string containing 'url(' inside params does not silently bypass validation.

issues.description: font-weight-notation prefilters use inconsistent case sensitivity and may misread mixed-value font shorthand.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED is case-insensitive while HAS_NUMERIC is case-sensitive, and neither isolates the weight token in the font shorthand. A value like '400 bold' contains both forms, so the fast-path conflates 'contains a keyword' with 'is keyword'. State and verify the invariant that the prefilter accepts every value the walker would flag, and pick one case stance.

issues.description: keyframe-selector-notation HAS_PERCENTAGE lacks the /i flag while HAS_KEYWORD has it, breaking prefilter symmetry.
issues.detail: PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS contents are digit-based so current cases pass, but the asymmetry is undocumented and risks future drift if keyword variants are added. State the invariant that the prefilter is a strict superset of cases the walker flags, and align case handling. Add a test for unusual whitespace (tabs/newlines) in keyframe selectors.

issues.description: Using /./ as a 'match everything' sentinel for walkRules is clever instead of obvious.
issues.detail: walkRules already accepts undefined to mean 'walk everything'. Branching on whether a filter exists and calling walkRules(filter, cb) or walkRules(cb) separates data from regex, eliminates the special case, and reads more clearly for the next maintainer.

issues.description: Regexes built from Sets/Maps interpolate contents without literal-escaping.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED, HAS_NUMERIC, HAS_PERCENTAGE, and HAS_KEYWORD join collection members directly into RegExp source. Current contents are alphanumeric/percent so it works, but if a future keyword contains a regex metacharacter the pattern silently corrupts. A small escapeRegExp helper at the join site makes the invariant hold by construction.

issues.description: Performance claim is unmeasured and the prefilter pattern is duplicated across six rules instead of lifted to data.
issues.detail: No before/after timings are provided for a six-file perf PR; a small benchmark would establish this is in the critical path. Additionally, each rule reinvents the same option-to-prefilter-regex guard inline with slightly different shapes. Lifting the mapping into a shared table or helper would make the pattern inspectable, testable, and uniform.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR's strategy — cheap string/regex prefilters before expensive parser walks across six *-notation rules — is sound and likely a real win. Two correctness concerns must be resolved before landing: the import-notation 'url' branch inverts its early-return and skips the very case it should validate, and font-weight-notation's prefilters mix case sensitivity while mishandling mixed-value font shorthand. Secondary issues include asymmetric case handling in keyframe-selector-notation, a /./ sentinel that should be undefined, unescaped regex construction from data, and a duplicated guard pattern that wants to be lifted into a shared table. Performance numbers should accompany the diff.
